content.title: About
content.content: Orange juice 100 % is a completely natural juice obtained from ripe oranges, frozen immediately after pressing and later reconstituted with water to its original volume. This processing preserves most of the vitamins and the fresh‑juice flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Freezing right after pressing retains up to 90 % of vitamin C, which degrades quickly in liquid juice.
Reconstituted juice tastes like fresh‑pressed juice but can be stored frozen for up to 12 months.
Orange juice is widely used in sauces, marinades, and desserts.
Juice from the ‘Valencia’ orange variety is considered the sweetest and most aromatic.
In the United States, more than 30 % of all frozen fruit juices are orange juice.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system, aids collagen synthesis, and acts as a powerful antioxidant.

items.title: Contains folate
items.content: Folate is essential for DNA synthesis and is especially important for pregnant women.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate blood pressure and supports heart function.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The juice contains virtually no fat, making it suitable for low‑calorie diets.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: In addition to vitamin C, the juice provides flavonoids that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Citrus allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to oranges.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: High acidity can irritate the stomach lining in people with gastritis or ulcers.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Although no sugar is added, natural sugars can affect blood glucose levels.

items.title: Vitamin loss with improper storage
items.content: If the juice is thawed and kept at room temperature for more than 24 hours, a portion of the vitamins degrades.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The juice can be enjoyed on its own, used in smoothies, cocktails, sauces, and marinades. When reconstituting, add clean water in a 1:1 volume ratio, mix thoroughly, and chill before serving.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the frozen juice at –18 °C in an airtight package. After thawing, keep it in the refrigerator for no more than 2‑3 days and consume within 24 hours of opening.
